what_it_does: Designs a wireless power transfer transmitter operating at 6.78 megahertz that maintains high efficiency (94.2 percent) across a wide range of receiving device charging states. Wireless charging efficiency typically drops when a device's charging characteristics (impedance) change; this circuit uses a Class-E power amplifier with dual adaptive impedance matching that independently adjusts both the real and imaginary components of impedance to keep the transmitter efficient. The system enables 33 watts of power transfer while minimizing wasted energy as heat.
